turn.user_message: ARPOB ₹8,000 a day. ALOS 6.5 days. Average daily revenue ₹28 lakhs. Bed occupancy 89%, ICU 94%. OT utilisation 75%, daily OT revenue ₹5 lakhs.

transcript.label: Transcript turn 15 · dead bed time turned into money
transcript.said: That’s everything I needed. The graphic below turns your dead bed time into a revenue number, step by step, so you can check every line of the arithmetic rather than take it from me. Two things I’ve deliberately left out of it: an ALOS gain on top, because that would be the same bed-days counted twice; and OT, which needs more from you before it can be sized honestly. Last question before we move on: has anyone worked out what your admissions desk can actually handle per hour at peak — counting internal bed transfers alongside admissions — or is that team sized by habit?

text: The steps turn your dead bed time into a revenue number, one line at a time. You can check every line rather than take it from me.
Two things I’ve left out on purpose. A shorter stay on top, because that would count the same days twice. And the operating theatre, which needs more from you first.
chat.note: ₹1.5 to 2 crore a year, from your own figures.

blocks.eyebrow: Dead bed time, turned into money
blocks.title: From one bed to a year
blocks.deck: Four steps, each worked out from your figures. Tap a step to see the working.

steps.label: Beds changing patient a day
steps.how: 267 beds, and each patient stays 6.5 days on average. 267 ÷ 6.5 is about 41.

steps.label: Hours won back each time
steps.how: Not all dead bed time can be won back. We count only the part a better plan can reach.

steps.label: Bed days won back a year
steps.how: 41 changes a day, 3 to 4 hours each, over 365 days. Divided by 24 hours, that is 1,900 to 2,500 days.

blocks.condition: This holds only if the freed hours can be filled. At 89% full, with patients waiting for beds, they can.

blocks.label: Revenue at stake
blocks.sub: At ₹8,000 a bed day. Your figures suggest that is the bed charge alone, so this understates the real amount.

blocks.label: A shorter average stay
blocks.sub: A shorter stay frees the same bed days. Adding it on top would count them twice.
